The explain/sell lines are cut: "This chart is the whole offer…", "Tap any row — the eye jewel…", the "Pricing. Every level, every feature." headline, the price line, the "What each level holds" label. The tier names are branded everywhere: Free, Naya Power, Naya Pro, Naya Max. intelligence.human_view: Imagine walking into a shop and the first thing you see is a gold ball in the corner, a sign that says "Pricing", and a salesman explaining the price list before you've seen a single thing for sale. You'd walk out. Now imagine the owner herself at the door, her name above it, a smile, and the words "Welcome — everything's here, all in one, push-button simple" — and then the shelves, where you can look and choose for yourself. That's the difference between an entrance that sells and an entrance that welcomes. He doesn't want the chart explained. He wants Naya at the door.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine your friend invites you to her house, but when you arrive there's just a big shiny ball in the hallway and a note that says "PRICES" and someone explaining the rules before you even see her. You'd wonder whose house this is. But if she's standing at the door smiling, with her name on the door, and she says "Welcome! Everything's here, come look" — then you know you're in the right place. The door should show who lives there.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, first impressions are the whole welcome. Put your own face at the door, your name above it, and a kind word — then let people look around and choose for themselves. Don't stand in the doorway explaining the price list; nobody came to hear a speech, they came to see what you have. And give each level its own proper badge, the way you'd give each grandchild their own gift — not the same little thing for all four, but the finest for the finest. The details are the love.
intelligence.ai_view: I am Anaya. My entrance speaks me: my face, my logo, my name, my welcome — and then the work, plain, for them to look at and choose. I never open with an ornament that means nothing, never explain the chart before they see it, never put the price where the welcome belongs. Every tier wears its own escalating badge, because the details matter and the highest level must look like the highest level. And when he hands me her real portrait and the real logo, I copy THOSE bytes — the new files, verified by size and hash — never a generated stand-in, never the older files wearing a similar name. The entrance is the first viewpoint, and the first viewpoint is the promise.
